subjects.name: Biology
subjects.definition: Biology is the branch of science that studies living organisms and life processes, including their structure, functions, growth, reproduction, evolution, and interactions with their environment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.definition: Chemistry is the branch of science concerned with matter, its composition, structure, properties, transformations, and associated energy changes.

subjects.name: Agricultural Science
subjects.definition: Agricultural science is the application of scientific principles to crop production, livestock management, soil science, farm tools, and agro-processing.

subjects.name: CRS
subjects.definition: Christian Religious Studies (CRS) is the study of biblical narratives, Christian teachings, ethics, faith, and the moral lessons drawn from the Old and New Testaments.
roadmap: The life and teachings of Jesus

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.definition: Mathematics is the science of numbers, quantity, structure, space, and change, used to solve problems through logical reasoning, proof, and calculation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.definition: Physics studies matter, energy, motion, forces, interactions, space, time, and the laws describing physical phenomena.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.definition: Computer science is the study of computers, computation, algorithms, data, and the practical and theoretical principles behind computing systems and software.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.definition: Geography is the study of Earth's physical environments, human societies, spatial relationships, and environmental interactions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.definition: Economics is the social science analyzing the allocation of scarce resources toward fulfilling unlimited human wants.

subjects.name: Government
subjects.definition: Government is the political organization or system through which a state or nation is governed and administered.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.definition: English Language covers grammar, vocabulary, comprehension, summary, parts of speech, concord, punctuation, figures of speech, and writing skills.

subjects.name: Literature
subjects.definition: Literature is the study of written works — prose, poetry, and drama — including their themes, plot, characterization, setting, tone, and literary devices.

subjects.name: General Knowledge
subjects.definition: General knowledge is broad, practical knowledge across science, technology, history, geography, civics, language, digital literacy, and everyday life.

formulas.name: Newton's Second Law
formulas.explanation: The net force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration. The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

formulas.name: Speed
formulas.explanation: Speed is the rate at which distance is covered. Its SI unit is metres per second (m/s).

formulas.name: Acceleration
formulas.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity per unit time, measured in m/s².

formulas.name: Momentum
formulas.explanation: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity, measured in kilogram-metres per second (kg·m/s).

formulas.name: Work

symbols.d: distance moved in the direction of the force

formulas.explanation: Work is energy transferred by a force acting through a distance, measured in joules (J).

formulas.name: Power
formulas.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, measured in watts (W).

formulas.name: Kinetic Energy
formulas.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion, measured in joules (J).

formulas.name: Gravitational Potential Energy
formulas.explanation: Gravitational potential energy is stored energy due to an object's position in a gravitational field.

formulas.name: Density
formulas.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume of a substance, measured in kg/m³ or g/cm³.

formulas.name: Pressure
formulas.explanation: Pressure is the force applied per unit area, measured in pascals (Pa).

formulas.name: Ohm's Law
formulas.explanation: Current through a conductor is proportional to voltage across it and inversely proportional to its resistance.

formulas.name: Quadratic Formula
formulas.explanation: The quadratic formula gives the solutions of ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

formulas.name: Pythagorean Theorem
formulas.explanation: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

formulas.name: Arithmetic Progression
formulas.explanation: The nth term of an arithmetic sequence where each term differs from the previous one by a constant d.

formulas.name: Geometric Progression
formulas.explanation: The nth term of a geometric sequence where each term is found by multiplying the previous one by a constant ratio r.

formulas.name: Probability
formulas.explanation: Probability measures the likelihood of an event occurring, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

formulas.name: Area of a Circle
formulas.explanation: The area of a circle is pi times the square of its radius.

formulas.name: Mole Calculation
formulas.explanation: The number of moles equals mass divided by molar mass. One mole contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles (Avogadro's constant).

misconceptions.misconception: Plants get all their food from soil.
misconceptions.correction: Plants obtain water and mineral nutrients from soil, but manufacture organic food through photosynthesis.

misconceptions.misconception: Osmosis and diffusion are the same thing.
misconceptions.correction: Diffusion is the movement of any particles from a region of high concentration to low concentration; osmosis is specifically the movement of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane.

misconceptions.misconception: Weight and mass are the same thing.
misconceptions.correction: Mass measures the amount of matter; weight is the gravitational force acting on an object.
Temperature describes thermal state; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.

misconceptions.misconception: Atoms cannot be broken down into smaller parts.
misconceptions.correction: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, but it is made of smaller particles: protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Plants respire day and night, breaking down glucose to release energy for growth and other life processes.

misconceptions.misconception: Only supply and demand determine prices in every market.
misconceptions.correction: Supply and demand are major price determinants, but government policy, production costs, competition, and other market structures also influence prices.
